comparator.name: Plant Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 105 EC of positive-credit compulsory common study (plus three zero-credit safety requirements), a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, an 18-EC bachelor thesis, one 24-EC specialisation and 30 EC of open electives. Plant Production and Ecology is selected because its official curriculum spans physiology, ecology, agronomy, agroecology, farming systems and technology and therefore best represents the broad applied plant-sciences identity; the choice is independent of UCR fit. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected by the official-order tie-break.
components: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Biology and Management of Plant Pests and Diseases
Resilience in Plant Sciences: Integrated Research From Molecules to Agro-ecosystems
Selected by official-order tie-break from the 3-EC mathematics/statistics restricted choice.
Agricultural Ecosystems - Linking Ecology, Agronomy & Rural Realities
Physiology and Development of Plants in Agriculture
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor requires one of two current 24-EC specialisations. Plant Production and Ecology spans plant physiology, ecology, agronomy, agroecology, farming systems and technology across organism and agroecosystem scales, while Plant Genomics and Health is the more narrowly molecular option. It therefore best represents the programme’s broad applied identity, independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Plant biology, agroecology & climate resilience
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum connects biology, physiology and laboratory work with ecology, sustainable farming, climate, water, soil and environmental research.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible plant-sciences response combining organismal and cellular biology with ecology, sustainable farming, climate resilience, environmental systems and quantitative research.
progression: Biology, ecology, sustainability and quantitative foundations precede evolution, molecular and physiological study, sustainable farming, environmental systems and applied research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from both earlier programmes by centring ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation and environmental change rather than molecular/biomedical mechanisms. It clears the 30-EC distinctness floor against each.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & genetic life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, physiology, laboratory research and computational analysis.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced plant-genomics and health direction through molecular and cell biology, genetics, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory research and biomedical data analysis.
progression: Life-science, programming, mathematics and laboratory foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, genetics, advanced biomedical science and quantitative analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction replaces most ecology, sustainable-farming, Earth-system and conservation study with molecular, cellular, genetic, biomedical and computational depth. It differs from the closest programme by well over four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Sustainable farming, food systems & governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum connects ecology and sustainable farming with food systems, economics, law, public policy, governance and societal change.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced plant-production, food-security and agroecology direction through ecology, sustainable farming, economics, law, governance, climate and applied sustainability research.
progression: Ecology, sustainability, politics, economics and quantitative foundations precede sustainable farming, environmental analysis, public law, governance and applied sustainability research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction gives food systems, economics, law, governance and societal decision-making a sustained role. It differs from both the biological closest programme and the molecular direction by well over four courses and 30 EC.

core: Plant biology, physiology, genetics, growth and health
Molecular and cellular plant science, biochemistry and biotechnology
Agronomy, agroecology, crop production, soils and farming systems
Ecology, biodiversity, environmental adaptation and climate resilience
Statistics, data science, modelling, experimental design and independent plant research
adjacent: Plant production, agroecology and resilient food systems
questions: How can crops supply healthy food while conserving nature and adapting to climate change?
How can genetics, molecular biology and biotechnology improve plant health and useful plant products?
How can ecology, data and field research improve resilient crop and agroecosystem design?

candidates.label: Plant production, agroecology & resilient food systems

selection.assessment: A broad plant-biology and agroecology programme is followed by two coherent, evidence-backed and mechanically feasible directions: molecular/cellular/genetic life sciences, and sustainable farming/food-systems governance. They are pairwise distinct by well over 30 EC, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated plant-sciences sequence with crop recognition, plant structure, plant pests and diseases, reproduction, photosynthesis, breeding, plant-focused laboratory and field research, a 24-EC specialisation and an 18-EC plant-sciences thesis. UCR can assemble substantial biology, ecology, sustainable farming, climate, data and governance study, but does not reproduce that specialist plant and crop sequence course for course.
